exposure: Robson Ten Group Classification System group
cohort: All women who delivered in Lithuania between January 1 and December 31, 2012 (n=25,373)
finding: The overall Caesarean section rate was 26.4%, with the largest contributions coming from nulliparous women with single cephalic full-term pregnancies (with or without labor induction) and multiparous women with a previous Caesarean section.
mod_finding: The study found that efforts to reduce the overall CS rate should focus on increasing vaginal birth after CS and reducing CS rates in nulliparous women with single cephalic full-term pregnancies.
